referenced_sources.title: Attention Lens: A Tool for Mechanistically Interpreting the Attention Head Information Retrieval Mechanism
referenced_sources.authors: Mansi Sakarvadia, Arham Khan, Aswathy Ajith, Daniel Grzenda, Nathaniel Hudson, André Bauer, Kyle Chard, Ian Foster
referenced_sources.abstract: Transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) are the state-of-the-art for natural language tasks. Recent work has attempted to decode, by reverse engineering the role of linear layers, the internal mechanisms by which LLMs arrive at their final predictions for text completion tasks. Yet little is known about the specific role of attention heads in producing the final token prediction. We propose Attention Lens, a tool that enables researchers to translate the outputs of attention heads into vocabulary tokens via learned attention-head-specific transformations called lenses. Preliminary findings from our trained lenses indicate that attention heads play highly specialized roles in language models.

referenced_sources.title: Mamba Knockout for Unraveling Factual Information Flow
referenced_sources.authors: Nir Endy, Idan Daniel Grosbard, Yuval Ran-Milo, Yonatan Slutzky, Itay Tshuva, Raja Giryes
referenced_sources.abstract: This paper investigates the flow of factual information in Mamba State-Space Model (SSM)-based language models. We rely on theoretical and empirical connections to Transformer-based architectures and their attention mechanisms. Exploiting this relationship, we adapt attentional interpretability techniques originally developed for Transformers to both Mamba-1 and Mamba-2. Using them we trace how information is transmitted and localized across tokens and layers.
